newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian stocks mixed, poised for growth.
newsitem.headline: Croatian stocks mixed, poised for growth.

text.p: Croatian stocks were mixed on Thursday with blue chips posting new but mild gains in slower trade, but market participants foresaw more activity and higher prices in the days ahead.
"We should not interpret the lull today as a beginning of a downward trend. I think the market has justed paused for breath after last week's bull run," one trader with a large market share said.
Another trader, Marijana Reskovac of Karlovacka Banka, said the market was stable after the elections and foreign investors, who have the largest influence on price trends, were coming back.
"Foreign investors...now see they don't have to fear any negative changes on the capital market," she said.
Meanwhile, the market awaited annual shareholders' meetings and profit announcements of major firms.
Drugs firm Pliva will release 1996 figures on Friday and Varazdinska Banka is holding an annual meeting on April 22.
Eight of 16 active issues rose on Thursday, six fell and two were flat. Volume was halved at 4,837 units, turnover shrank to 2.8 million kuna from 10 million.
Fully-listed Zagrebacka Banka rose 11.25 kuna to 2,011.45, selling 625 shares.
"Demand for Zagrebacka's shares is high but offer is scarce. Shareholders seem to be waiting for their dividend," one trader said, adding the stock could dip further to fluctuate around 2,000 kuna.
The bank's C-series bearer shares lost 20 kuna to 780, with only one share sold and its E-series preference stock added 19 kuna to 1,020.

Varazdinska's first issue, recently listed in the top bracket of the Zagreb bourse, sold only one share for 46,000, up 1,000 from Wednesday. Its second issue lost 90 kuna to 1,360, with four units changing hands.
Traders said Varazdinska, especially its first issue, was definitely heading for a correction.
Fully-listed Pliva inched up one kuna to 479 on volume of 40 units.
Biggest gainer hotelier Arenaturist added seven kuna or 5.18 percent to 142 kuna, with 141 units sold.
Top loser was hotelier Riviera Porec, dipping 15 kuna or 8.57 percent to 160 on volume of 351 shares.
Food processor Podravka was most actively traded stock with 2,527 shares, closing one kuna lower at 307.
